ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
There is a right-angled $\mathrm{V}$-shaped groove fixed on a horizontal plane, with its cross-section as shown in the figure. The angle between the BC surface and the horizontal plane is $60^{\circ}$. A uniform wooden cube with mass $\mathbf{m}$ is placed inside the groove, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the cube and the AB surface, as well as the BC surface, is $\upmu$. A force perpendicular to the plane of the paper and directed inward is applied to push the cube to move along the groove.

1. Determine the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the wooden block.
2. Determine the direction of the frictional force acting on the wooden block.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2}\upmu\mathrm{mg}$
The direction is perpendicular to the plane of the paper, pointing outward.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows the cross section of a right-angle V-shaped groove fixed on a horizontal surface, with the two groove faces intersecting at point B near the bottom. The right groove face is labeled BC, and the figure marks its angle with the horizontal plane as 60°; the left groove face is labeled AB, and the figure marks its angle with the horizontal plane as 30°. The wooden block is located between the two inclined planes and is simultaneously in contact with face AB and face BC, and is pushed by a force along the direction perpendicular to the paper surface to move along the groove. Reasoning: Take the horizontal rightward direction in the paper plane as the x-axis, and the vertical upward direction as the y-axis. Let the normal force exerted by face AB on the wooden block be N_AB, and the normal force exerted by face BC on the wooden block be N_BC. Since the normal force is perpendicular to the contact surface, the normal force of face AB points to the upper right, making an angle of 60° with the positive horizontal axis; the normal force of face BC points to the upper left, making an angle of 150° with the positive horizontal axis. The wooden block has no acceleration in the cross section of the paper plane, therefore the forces in the paper plane are balanced. Horizontal direction equilibrium: N_AB cos60° + N_BC cos150° = 0. Vertical direction equilibrium: N_AB sin60° + N_BC sin150° = mg. Substituting cos60°=1/2, cos150°=-√3/2, sin60°=√3/2, sin150°=1/2: (1/2)N_AB - (√3/2)N_BC = 0, so N_AB = √3 N_BC. (√3/2)N_AB + (1/2)N_BC = mg. Substituting gives (√3/2)(√3 N_BC)+(1/2)N_BC=mg, namely 2N_BC=mg, so N_BC=mg/2, N_AB=√3mg/2. The magnitudes of the kinetic friction forces on the two contact surfaces are respectively μN_AB and μN_BC, and both are along the groove direction. The magnitude of the total friction force is μN_AB+μN_BC = μ(√3mg/2+mg/2)=((1+√3)/2)μmg. The external force pushes the wooden block inward along the direction perpendicular to the paper surface, making the wooden block have a tendency to slide inward relative to the two contact surfaces; therefore the two kinetic friction forces both hinder this motion, their directions are both perpendicular to the paper surface outward, and the resultant friction force is also perpendicular to the paper surface outward.
